brief.purpose: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions by proving Swing Shack's TrackMan technology gives golfers data-driven insight their game has been missing.
brief.audience: Jozi golfers, 25-50, mid-high handicap. They track their fitness — they want to track their golf. Data-aware, skeptical of voodoo tips, willing to pay for evidence-based improvement.
brief.bigIdea: Your swing has a number. TrackMan measures it. That number is the shortcut to better scores.
brief.successMetric: Fitting sessions booked. Secondary: GMB posts live weekly. Tertiary: engagement rate on stat-hook content above 2.5%.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A hook that stops the scroll with a specific number. A visual that shows TrackMan data overlaid on a club or swing. A caption that earns the click by expanding the data story. Booking link front and centre.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Vague transformation claims ('From confused golfer to confident striker'). Busy backgrounds without contrast. Price-led content without data justification. Anything that looks like generic golf marketing.

dna.tone: Clinical authority. Data speaks, we just translate it. No hype, no fluff — numbers are the argument. Authoritative but not cold. Expert without being gatekeeping.
dna.contentMix: 70% educational (data insights, stats explainers) / 20% promotional (session offers, fitting deals) / 10% social proof (client results, before/after)
forbiddenVisualStyles: text over busy backgrounds without contrast layer
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Direct price-led with anchoring: show the value first (TrackMan data), then introduce the offer. Always include R-amount. 'From R250' works because the data has already justified the price.

platformStrategy.instagram: Stat-first hook stops the scroll. Data overlay on image tells the story. Caption expands with context. Link in bio drives booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the number/stat itself. 'Your drive: 199m' as text overlay. 3-second hook, then explain the data. Fast-cut, punchy.
platformStrategy.gmb: Trust + proof + convenience. Service highlight with one key stat. Clean, professional, no gimmicks. Call to action is always 'book now' or 'call us'.

exampleHighPerforming.whyItWorked: 'Your golf stats don't lie' — specific, implies measurement, triggers curiosity about what the stats reveal. Stats hooks 2.5x better than transformation hooks.

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: 'FROM CONFUSED GOLFER TO CONFIDENT STRIKER' — vague, no data anchor. Transformation claims without proof feel empty.

bestHooks.notes: Stats angle consistently outperforms transformation. 'Your [metric]' format is the winner.

failedContent.reason: Vague transformation claim, no data anchor
failedContent.lesson: Always lead with a number or specific stat. 'Your [X]' outperforms 'FROM [state] TO [state]'
Weather/indoor convenience is table stakes, not a hook. Stats create urgency.

lessonsLearned: Stats hooks consistently outperform all other angles — lead with numbers always

brief.purpose: Keep Swing Shack bookings steady through SA winter by positioning indoor golf as the obvious choice when outdoor courses go cold.
brief.audience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who stop playing in winter because their home course gets cold or they travel less. They already have clubs — they just need a reason to keep playing.
brief.bigIdea: Winter doesn't exist in here. (It's always 22°C, there's food and drinks, and the simulator never closes.)
brief.successMetric: Winter session bookings vs prior year. Secondary: winter package upsells. Tertiary: social engagement on contrast-style content.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A visual that makes you want to be inside — warm lights, green fairways on screen, something cold and grey outside the window. A hook that names the weather or the day. Content that feels like a friend saying 'actually, this is good.'
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Clinical data overlays. Golf swing technique photos. Anything that makes indoor golf sound like a chore or a substitute. Content that positions winter as a problem rather than Swing Shack as the answer.

visualDirection.mood: Dark theater with a spotlight on uncomfortable truths and golden salvation.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Open with pitch-black backgrounds where a single club or piece of equipment sits under dramatic lighting — isolated, exposed, wrong. Contrast this immediately with split-screen moments showing the absurdity: a driver used to putt, a putter used off the tee, a recreational golfer wielding a stiff-shaft blade meant for single-digit handicaps. The solution moments break this darkness with warm gold highlights — custom fitting rooms, hands measuring grip size, clubs being dialed in. The golfer should feel seen and slightly called out, then immediately relieved that there's a clear path forward.
imageReferences: a golfer squinting down at a 4-iron that clearly belongs in a pro's bag
the dramatic pause before a shank, lit with urgency
a fitting session where the clubhead finally matches the swing speed
visualDirection.colorUsage: The near-black background creates theatrical tension and forces the eye to focus on the equipment being critiqued — nothing is hidden. The warm orange primary (#FF6B35) functions as the 'you're doing this wrong' signal — it grabs attention and creates urgency without feeling aggressive. Gold (#D4AF37) only appears at the moment of solution, making it feel earned and premium — the golfer has graduated from problem to fix. This hierarchy matches the campaign's emotional arc from discomfort to resolution.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines that hit hard and fast — think impact statements like 'THIS IS YOUR 7-IRON.' Clean, readable body text that doesn't compete with the visual drama. The contrast between aggressive headlines and calm explanation mirrors the tone.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Vertical video dominates on Instagram — use the full frame for maximum emotional impact. For static posts, lean into asymmetry — equipment slightly off-center, text anchored to one side, letting the imagery breathe in the negative space of the dark background.
contentExamples: Reel: Side-by-side — professional trying to use kitchen scissors to cut a steak, then same energy as a weekend golfer using a blade iron meant for scratch players
Carousel: '5 Signs Your Clubs Are Wrong For You' — each slide dark with orange warning, gold solution icon at the end linking to booking
Story sequence: Poll asking 'Do you know your swing speed?' then revealing the irony of mismatched equipment, ending with booking link

pillars.name: The Absurdity Mirror — Name Your Equipment Sin
pillars.description: This pillar owns the provocative hook. It confronts golfers with the obvious absurdity of their equipment choices using relatable wrong-tool analogies. Strategic job: Stop the scroll, create recognition, make them feel seen. Every post under this pillar should make the golfer laugh (in recognition) and then wince (in realization). Pure attention-grab, no pitch yet.

pillars.name: The Hidden Performance Cost — What Wrong Clubs Steal From You
pillars.description: This pillar owns the consequence layer. It educates on exactly what poor equipment costs — distance loss, consistency sacrifice, injury risk, frustration accumulation. Strategic job: Build the emotional case for change by quantifying the pain of staying the same. Moves the golfer from 'that's funny' to 'that's me' to 'I need to fix this.' Proof and specificity are non-negotiable here.

pillars.name: The Fitting Revelation — Education as the Path to Trust
pillars.description: This pillar owns the 'how we solve it' moment. It demystifies club fitting — what actually happens, why it matters, what gets measured (swing speed, launch angle, shaft flex, lie angle). Strategic job: Transform the fitting from intimidating unknown to exciting opportunity. Position our expertise as the bridge from frustration to performance. Educate without overwhelming; intrigue, don't lecture.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — Real Johannesburg Golfer Results
pillars.description: This pillar owns social proof and emotional payoff. It showcases real golfers (Johannesburg locals if possible) whose games transformed after fitting. Strategic job: Make the solution feel tangible, achievable, and real. Show the before-after journey — not just better scores, but the feeling of confidence, consistency, and enjoyment returning. This is the emotional release after the confrontation.

pillars.name: The Obvious Next Step — Book Your Session
pillars.description: This pillar owns conversion action. Every post, story, and reel ultimately funnels here — the clear, warm invitation to book a fitting or practice session. Strategic job: Make saying 'yes' feel like the obvious, easy, overdue decision. Remove friction, create urgency where appropriate, and ensure every piece of content has a clear on-ramp to booking. The CTA isn't a push — it's the helpful conclusion to a story that needed telling.
